idiom_name: coordinator object with a dict of view factories and weakref-friendly open views
implementation_notes: Python's own data structures carry the pattern: a coordinator holds a dict from view id to view object or factory, its open/close methods maintain that dict, and the change fan-out is an observer list of callables or bound methods walked in a loop. What replaces the classic structure is the absence of ceremony - views are plain objects or tkinter widgets, creation by type is factories[type](model), switching in a Tk UI is ttk.Notebook's tab selection (or a frame swap), and dict/list comprehensions do the registry bookkeeping the classic form hides behind classes. The class form is still justified - and is exactly the POSA shape, only lighter - when several view types are registered dynamically and meta-operations act on the whole set; add weak references (weakref.WeakSet, weakref.ref) so the registry and the widgets' callbacks do not keep closed views alive.
pitfalls: Tk widgets may only be touched from the thread that runs the mainloop: a model change produced by a worker thread must be marshalled with root.after(0, ...) or a queue, or Tkinter raises or corrupts the event state.
A registry of weak references is not enough when the view also holds a strong reference to the model's callback list - the cycle keeps it alive - so close() must unregister the callbacks as well.
Tkinter variables and images that are referenced only from a local scope can be garbage-collected and blank the widget; keep the reference on the owning widget or in the handler.
Forgetting .destroy() on a closed Tk widget leaks the native window and its callbacks even after the Python object is dropped from the registry.
